_comment: Erin's Garden of Sanctuary -- the ONE map with no darkness, no walls, no violence. Formal south-to-north axis per the direction card: `garden_exit` (the vine door, the only way in or out) -> the sandstone path -> the statue-fountain centerpiece -> the misted rise (an open band at the north end -- populating it with memorial plinths/statues via visual_states is a future task's job; this ships the CLEARING only, no memorial entities yet). `biome: garden` (data/biomes.json) supplies the olive-grass floor + the hedge-hem `blocked` tile + the owned PixelLab sky-mist skirt (the impossible bright sky beyond the hedge). 14x12: small and serene by design, 'a small serene map off the inn'. Reachability: `garden_exit` (7,11) is the sole hedge gap; every other perimeter cell is hedge-blocked. The fountain (7,6) sits ON the path axis and is the map's only interior obstacle -- a 1-cell detour left/right (both open floor) routes around it, matching a real garden path splitting around a centerpiece; no BFS pinch point exists (confirmed: the only blocked cells are the perimeter ring + this one center cell). `garden_bed` (11,4, east wing) is the rest-anywhere-equivalent bed, 'facing the rise' per handoff.md's own recommendation -- a literal bed under the open sky is the map's 'rest anywhere' read, not a mismatch. Mood: data/moods.json's `garden` card (identity-at-every-phase, vignette 0.0 -- the ONLY such card in the game). No `arena_moods` entry (combat impossible here, the sim guard in wi_game.gd's start_combat) and no `walls` field at all (the Garden ships NO wall family by design -- sanctuary is the absence of architecture; the hedge hem is expressed entirely via `blocked` + the biome's own hedge tile, the exact same mechanism inn/floodplains/etc use for their `blocked` cells, just with zero `walls.segments` on top).

floor_layers._comment: The formal north-south path axis (direction.md: 'one straight line of meaning'). Sandstone family per picks.md §1b, position-hashed variants (the inn plank-floor idiom). Skips (7,6) -- the fountain's own cell, painted by the base grass floor underneath its decor sprite instead.

The misted rise (direction.md: 'an arc of colorless statues standing in a band of white mist at the axis head'). G1 ships the CLEARING only -- a lighter grass variant marking the band, no statues/plinths yet (G2's memorial seam). One row south of the north hedge so a future plinth row has open floor to stand on.

decor._comment: The statue-fountain composite (picks.md §2, resolving the 8a §5 deferral): basin FIRST, statue SECOND -- both licensed Pixel Crawler crops (placeholder-rendering until the controller lands the assets/props/garden/Feminine-Idle-Sheet.png manifest entry; see the G1 report). THE BLOCKING CONTRACT: (7,6) is in this map's own `blocked` list above (the boulder/ruin_surface precedent -- a decor-only 'solid' object is a real bug).

entities._comment: The way back to the inn -- pairs with `garden_door` (inn map, cell 3,6). Landing (3,7) is one cell south of that door, the sewer_exit/deep_fissure/ruin_exit 'never land on the door's own cell' convention. `garden_door_inner` reused verbatim (one physical door, two faces). Ungated (a real `door`, always open from this side -- the K-of-N gate lives entirely on the inn-side prop).

The rest-anywhere-equivalent bed (spec §5's mechanical surface list). Same `sleep()` call, same progression/toast machinery as every other bed (the inn_upstairs your_bed precedent) -- the ONE authored difference is `sleep_toast`, an additional flavor line emitted BEFORE sleep()'s own stream, never replacing it.
entities.observe: Someone carried a real bed out here, onto real grass, under a sky that isn't real. It's made up with clean linen anyway, like that settles the argument.
entities.sleep_toast: Somewhere, a door shuts softly. The garden doesn't dim.

entities._comment: The memorial hill -- four plots on the misted-rise band (y=1, direction.md/handoff.md's memorial vocabulary), one per owned stone-ified statue in the roster (human/gnoll/drake/goblin, pixellab-batch.md), spaced at x=4/6/8/10 flanking the path axis (x=7, left open as the arc's own center per direction.md landmark 3). Canon: the sacred hill of statues Ch. 7.11 ('but for color they could have turned and greeted you') -- game simplification per handoff.md open question 2, one shared roster rather than per-viewer. Each plot is the dirty_table/unlit_lantern visual_states idiom EXACTLY (base sprite `memorial_plinth`, a single `{counter,at:1}` state swapping to its statue) with ONE addition this task needed and wi_game.gd now carries (`_resolve_observe_text`, doc-commented there): the SAME visual_states list also carries an optional `observe` override, so [Appraise Foe]'s existing single-string read shows the base plinth's 'waiting' flavor before the beat and the statue's own results-only remembrance line after -- proven live by garden_walkthrough (one plot pre-banked via the fixture's own resolved_wrong_order leg, present; one plot's counter genuinely unbanked, absent -- the negative tooth). Spoiler cutoff: every remembrance line stays Vol 1-7, no character named, deeds only -- the roster itself is deliberately race-generic (direction.md vocabulary point 5), the remembrance TEXT carries the specific memory, never the sprite. Memorial statues NEVER reuse a living NPC's colored sprite (the repo's known indistinguishable-prop failure mode) -- every one of these four is the ONE stoneify.py ramp, guaranteeing colorless memorial stone regardless of source figure.
entities.observe: A stone plinth, swept clean, facing the axis like the others. Whatever belongs here hasn't been carried up from below yet.

visual_states.observe: A gnoll carved in stone, sword low and steady, facing down toward where the path forgets itself. Something old came up from under Liscor once. Something else went down after it, and came back up alone. The warren has been quiet since.

entities._comment: The seal beat's own counter -- Zevara's 'It's done. The thing under the city won't be climbing up.' hub option (zevara_intro.json), gated on `cleared_the_warren` and banking `raskghar_sealed` (the Act III advance key, traced from data, not assumed) -- a DISTINCT beat from the boss victory itself (this plot's neighbor), the political/civic resolution rather than the fight.
entities.observe: An empty plinth near the row's center, the mist pooling faintly at its base as if it expects company.

visual_states.observe: A drake in stone, spear planted, watching over ground that used to worry the whole city. Liscor sealed the dark for good, once the warren was cleared -- masonry over memory, and no one asked for thanks. This is as close as the hill gets to giving one anyway.

entities._comment: The Wrong Order's shared convergence counter (quests.json beat 'resolve') -- ALSO one of `near_garden`'s own two pre-banked K-of-4 legs (wi_game.gd's `_garden_earn_met`), so this plot ships PRESENT from the fixture's own load in garden_walkthrough, no extra live-banking needed to prove the swap (the counter genuinely met, read live through the exact same visual_states/`_resolve_observe_text` seam as every other plot).
entities.observe: A stone plinth at the far end of the row, otherwise unremarkable, waiting on whatever the inn hasn't settled yet.

visual_states.observe: A human figure in stone, apron tied, a bowl held out in both hands like an offering that never quite finished being made. The inn came up short once. Nobody outside its walls ever had to know.

entities._comment: The fourth plot -- `goblins_spared` (#26) is now live, banked by `goblin_parley`'s 'Stand aside' bypass; this plot renders as the waiting plinth for any save that never took that branch and swaps to `memorial_statue_goblin` once the counter is >= 1, zero further code/data changes needed here. Doubles as direction.md's 'the hill always waits' promise: even once all three OTHER plots claim their statues, the arc never reads as full for a save that fought every goblin.
entities.observe: A bare stone plinth at the end of the row, angled slightly wide of the others -- room left on purpose. Nothing stands on it yet. The mist doesn't seem to mind waiting.

visual_states.observe: A goblin carved in stone, unarmed, hands open at its sides. Not every ending here was a fight. This one is remembered for not being one.
